articles.title: What is GDP and how fast is the UK economy growing?
articles.summary: The rate of UK economic growth affects things like pay increases and the amount of tax raised.
articles.body:
Investment in artificial intelligence (AI) helped to drive a surprise boost in the UK economy in July, according to official figures.

Economic growth matters because it affects things like pay increases for workers and the amount of tax the government raises to pay for services.

UK economic growth is measured by the change in the country's GDP, or gross domestic product. This includes all the economic activity of companies, governments, and people in a country.

In the UK, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) publishes new GDP figures every month . However, these can vary quite a lot and the quarterly figures – covering three months at a time – are considered more significant.

Most economists, politicians, and businesses like to see GDP rising steadily.

That's because it usually means people are spending more, extra jobs are created, more tax is paid, and workers get better pay rises.

When GDP is falling, it means the economy is shrinking.

This can be bad news for businesses and workers as it can lead to pay freezes and job losses.

If GDP falls for two quarters in a row, that is known as a recession .

The economy expanded by 0.4% in July, the ONS said, whereas economists had predicted no growth.

It follows growth of 0.3% in June and zero growth in May.

Economists said July's surprise growth figure showed the UK economy was proving resilient in the face of shocks, such as the US-Israel war with Iran.

The outbreak of the conflict has led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway south of Iran through which one fifth of the world's oil and gas usually flows.

This closure has led to a sharp jump in oil prices, which has fed through to higher energy and fuel prices.

Economists expect UK growth to slow in the months ahead as those costs continue to affect households and businesses.

However, the IMF currently forecasts the UK's economy will grow by 1% this year , up from its previous estimate of 0.8%.

The Labour government has repeatedly said growth is its top priority, but has faced criticism for achieving only moderate GDP growth since it took power in 2024.

The ONS has estimated UK GDP increased by 1.3% in 2025 , up from 1.0% in 2024.

UK growth forecast upgraded by IMF but risks remain

How the Iran war affects your money and bills

How does GDP affect tax and public services?

If GDP is going up steadily, people pay more in tax because they're earning and spending more.

This means more money for the government, which it can choose to spend on public services, such as schools, police, and hospitals.

When the economy shrinks and a country goes into recession, these things can go into reverse.

Governments tend to get less money in tax, which means they may decide to freeze or cut public spending, or put taxes up.

In 2020, the Covid pandemic caused the most severe UK recession for more than 300 years. In response, the government borrowed hundreds of billions of pounds to support the economy.

Output: The total value of goods and services produced by all sectors of the economy – agriculture, manufacturing, energy, construction, the service sector, and government.

Expenditure: The value of goods and services bought by households and by government as well as investment in machinery and buildings. It also includes the value of exports, minus imports.

Income: The value of the income generated, mostly in terms of profits and wages.

In the UK, the ONS publishes one single measure of GDP, which is calculated using all three measurements.

But early estimates mainly use the output measure, using data collected from thousands of companies.

Why does the GDP figure sometimes change?

The UK produces one of the quickest estimates of GDP of the major economies, about 40 days after the quarter in question.

At that stage, only about 60% of the data is available, so the figure is revised as more information comes in.

The ONS publishes more information about this on its website .

What are the limitations of the GDP figure?

GDP is not the whole story as it does not include several things :

The hidden economy: Unpaid work such as caring for children or elderly relatives isn't captured.

Inequality: Rising GDP could result from the richest getting richer, rather than everyone becoming better off, and some people could be worse off.

Living standards: If the population is also growing, increased GDP can still mean less money per person, which can reduce people's living standards. This is why the GDP per capita measure is important.

Some critics also argue that GDP doesn't take into account whether the economic growth it measures is sustainable, or the environmental damage it might do.

Alternative measures have been developed which try to capture this.

Since 2010, the ONS has also measured well-being alongside economic growth. This assesses health, relationships, education and skills, as well as people's personal finances and the environment.

But despite its limitations, GDP is still the most widely used measure for most government decisions and international comparisons.

articles.title: CM Vijay skips VIP gate at Chennai airport after advisor denied special entry for London trip
articles.summary: CHENNAI: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay is set to skip the VIP entry into Chennai airport via Gate 6 and will enter through the regular T2 internationa.
articles.body: CHENNAI: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay is set to skip the VIP entry into Chennai airport via Gate 6 and will enter through the regular T2 international terminal like other passengers to fly to London, after the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) denied entry to his advisor Vishnu Reddy, who is accompanying the CM on his maiden overseas visit to woo investments, citing security reasons.Airport sources said only the President and Prime Minister are eligible for ceremonial entry into the airport, while the facility is extended to the chief minister and governor of the particular state on special request.While the chief minister's office made a request for special entry for the chief minister on Thursday, BCAS accepted it but said that persons accompanying the VIP should enter through the regular international terminal as per protocol.However, the chief minister reportedly refused to use the VIP gate only for himself and decided to enter the airport like other international passengers.After receiving the information, airport authorities made arrangements to usher in the guests through Gate No. D9, which is used only for emergencies. articles.title: Influenciadora que fazia vídeos comendo grandes quantidades de comida morre na China | G1
articles.standfirst: Chen Ziyi, de 24 anos, era conhecida como Ganfan Yingying e fazia transmissões ao vivo consumindo volumes excessivos de alimentos. Informações sobre sua morte foram divulgadas por veículos de notícia chineses.
articles.summary: Chen Ziyi, de 24 anos, era conhecida como Ganfan Yingying e fazia transmissões ao vivo consumindo volumes excessivos de alimentos. Informações sobre sua morte foram divulgadas por veículos de notícia chineses.
articles.body:
Ganfan Yingying aparece em vídeos de mukbang — Foto: Douyin

Uma influenciadora chinesa Chen Ziyi, de 24 anos, conhecida na internet como Ganfan Yingying , morreu após sofrer uma parada cardíaca supostamente relacionada a baixos níveis de potássio no sangue. As informações foram divulgadas por veículos de notícia chineses.

Yingying fazia transmissões ao vivo de mukbang, formato de conteúdo em que influenciadores comem grandes quantidades de comida diante das câmeras.

Segundo os relatos, Yingyin morreu em 17 de agosto. Os pais dela anunciaram a morte nas redes sociais na última sexta-feira (4). A influenciadora tinha mais de 1 milhão de seguidores.

Influenciadora que comia dezenas de alimentos em transmissões morre aos 24 anos na China — Foto: Global Times

Ainda de acordo com informações divulgadas por veículos chineses, em seu último vídeo, publicado em 14 de agosto, ela contou que episódios repetidos de alimentação excessiva haviam provocado uma queda nos níveis de potássio e levado à sua hospitalização. Segundo a influenciadora, a concentração de potássio no sangue chegou a 2,3.

Chen afirmou que os problemas de saúde estavam relacionados às atividades que realizava nas transmissões. Ela também contou que já havia sido hospitalizada anteriormente pelo mesmo motivo e mencionou um antigo hábito de provocar o próprio vômito.

No vídeo, a influenciadora afirmou ainda que, "embora ganhar dinheiro fosse importante, a saúde deveria estar em primeiro lugar".

Yingying afirmou ainda que as transmissões podiam ser fisicamente desgastantes. Em uma delas, disse ter precisado comer entre 60 e 70 ovos em conserva. Segundo ela, alguns produtos exigiam que os influenciadores continuassem comendo durante as transmissões. Ela disse que os mukbangers sofrem pressão para consumir quantidades cada vez maiores de comida para aumentar as vendas, mesmo quando o corpo já não suporta o esforço.

China tem regras contra consumo excessivo em transmissões

A China possui regras para restringir conteúdos de transmissões ao vivo que promovam o consumo excessivo de alimentos.

A Lei de Combate ao Desperdício de Alimentos, aprovada em 2021, proíbe a produção, publicação e disseminação de conteúdos de áudio e vídeo que promovam o consumo excessivo e a compulsão alimentar.

Um código de conduta para streamers online, publicado em 2022, também proíbe práticas como simular que está comendo, provocar vômito e comer compulsivamente durante transmissões, segundo veículos de notícia chineses.

articles.title: Servidor teria feito 561 viagens por app durante expediente | G1
articles.standfirst: Cruzamento de dados analisado pela Promotoria encontrou coincidências entre deslocamentos remunerados e registros de presença em pelo menos 134 dias.
articles.summary: Cruzamento de dados analisado pela Promotoria encontrou coincidências entre deslocamentos remunerados e registros de presença em pelo menos 134 dias.
articles.body:
O servidor público suspeito de descumprir a jornada de trabalho na Prefeitura de Porto Nacional enquanto exercia atividade remunerada como motorista de aplicativo realizou pelo menos 561 viagens.

De acordo com o Ministério Público do Tocantins (MPTO), o cruzamento das informações apontou coincidência, em pelo menos 134 dias de trabalho, entre viagens remuneradas realizadas em Palmas e horários registrados como expediente.

O levantamento identificou um total de 267 horas e 30 minutos de atividade privada durante a jornada de trabalho. Em 15 dias, essa atividade teria ocupado mais de seis horas do expediente.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

O órgão recomendou que a prefeitura instaure um Processo Administrativo Disciplinar (PAD) para apurar a conduta do servidor, lotado na Secretaria Municipal de Educação.

Em nota, a Secretaria Municipal de Educação afirmou que irá adotar as providências para instauração do processo disciplinar. Informou que irá garantir ao servidor o direito ao contraditório e ampla defesa e que, caso a apuração comprove irregularidade e eventual dano ao erário, serão adotadas medidas administrativas e legais cabíveis, incluindo o ressarcimento de valores (veja a nota abaixo) .

Prefeitura de Porto Nacional — Foto: Djavan Barbosa/Jornal do Tocantins

O caso passou a ser investigado após o MPTO receber uma denúncia de descumprimento de jornada de trabalho. O histórico de uma conta de aplicativo de transporte e as folhas de ponto do servidor, assinadas pelo servidor entre fevereiro de 2023 e maio de 2026, foram examinadas e confrontadas.

Na recomendação, o Ministério Público ressalta que os elementos reunidos têm natureza indiciária e não representam conclusão definitiva sobre a conduta do investigado. O órgão destaca que qualquer responsabilização depende de apuração que garanta o contraditório e a ampla defesa.

MPTO, a folha de ponto no município funciona em sistema de formulário manuscrito e que, entre fevereiro a maio de 2026, o investigado foi responsável por atestar a própria frequência.

Por isso, foi determinado um prazo de 15 dias para que a Prefeitura de Porto Nacional instaure o processo para apurar:

Quem realizou o preenchimento das folhas do servidor;

Existência ou inexistência de autorização, comunicação ou ciência da administração quanto ao exercício de atividade privada;

Compatibilidade entre a atividade privada exercida e o regime de trabalho, jornada e as vedações aplicáveis ao cargo;

Conduta das chefias imediatas responsáveis pelo atesto das folhas de ponto em cada período;

A circunstância de o servidor haver atestado a própria frequência na condição de Diretor de Unidade Escolar;

Quantificação de eventual valor pago sem a correspondente contraprestação de serviço.

O município foi recomendado a avaliar a implantação de marcação eletrônica ou biométrica de frequência nas unidades da rede municipal de ensino, ou, que reveja o procedimento de preenchimento, conferência e atesto das folhas de ponto manuscritas.

O órgão também pediu a verificação da existência de autorização, comunicação ou conhecimento da administração municipal sobre o exercício de atividade privada remunerada pelo servidor, bem como a compatibilidade dessa atividade com o cargo ocupado e as regras previstas na legislação municipal.

Nota da Secretaria Municipal de Educação

A Prefeitura de Porto Nacional recebeu a recomendação expedida pelo Ministério Público do Tocantins e adotará as providências administrativas necessárias para a instauração de Processo Administrativo Disciplinar (PAD).

Em etapa anterior, a Secretaria Municipal de Educação já havia sido notificada sobre a denúncia e solicitou esclarecimentos ao servidor citado. Na ocasião, foi apresentada defesa prévia, posteriormente encaminhada ao Ministério Público. Após a análise inicial, o órgão ministerial solicitou informações complementares diretamente ao servidor e, em seguida, expediu a recomendação ao Município.

O PAD garantirá ao servidor o direito ao contraditório e à ampla defesa. Durante o procedimento, serão analisadas as folhas de frequência, os registros mencionados pelo Ministério Público, a documentação apresentada pelo servidor e os demais elementos relacionados ao caso.

Neste momento, ainda não é possível afirmar se houve responsabilidade funcional ou prejuízo aos cofres públicos. Caso a apuração comprove alguma irregularidade e eventual dano ao erário, serão adotadas as medidas administrativas e legais cabíveis, incluindo o ressarcimento dos valores apurados.

A administração municipal tomou conhecimento da possível realização de atividade privada durante o expediente por meio da denúncia e do procedimento conduzido pelo Ministério Público. Os dados obtidos pelo órgão ministerial serão considerados na apuração, sem antecipação de responsabilidade antes da conclusão do processo administrativo.

Sem prejuízo dos mecanismos atualmente utilizados nas unidades escolares, a possibilidade de aperfeiçoamento do controle de frequência, inclusive por meio de sistemas eletrônicos ou biométricos, será objeto de avaliação técnica e administrativa pela Secretaria Municipal de Educação.

articles.title: Tempestade no interior de SP causa acidente com mortes e cancela aulas | G1
articles.standfirst: Duas pessoas morreram após um carro aquaplanar e bater em um caminhão em Avaré (SP), na quinta-feira (10). A Defesa Civil informou que Piraju (SP) teve a maior rajada de vento de SP, com 88 km/h.
articles.summary: Uma tempestade na quinta-feira (10) provocou acidentes com mortes, alagamentos e suspensão de aulas no interior paulista. Duas pessoas morreram em em Avaré (SP).
articles.body:
A tempestade que atingiu diversas cidades nesta quinta-feira (10) causou acidente com mortes, enchentes e o cancelamento de aulas na região de Itapetininga (SP).

Avaré (SP) foi a cidade mais atingida pela chuva , com um acidente que deixou duas mortes na Rodovia João Mellão (SP-255) após um carro aquaplanar e bater de frente com um caminhão . Em Itapetininga (SP), uma estrada vicinal cedeu após o alto volume de água. Assista ao vídeo acima.

Já em Piraju (SP), a Defesa Civil de São Paulo informou que foi a cidade com a maior rajada de vento do dia, com 88 quilômetros por hora. O g1 preparou uma reportagem mostrando os estragos causados pela tempestade na região de Itapetininga. Confira abaixo:

Um acidente envolvendo um caminhão e um carro causou duas mortes e deixou outras duas pessoas feridas na Rodovia João Mellão (SP-255). Segundo a Defesa Civil municipal, foram registrados 85 milímetros de chuva nas últimas 24 horas.

Testemunhas relataram ao Corpo de Bombeiros que o carro aquaplanou na pista devido à forte chuva que atingia a cidade e bateu de frente com o caminhão.

Além dos dois mortos, uma pessoa foi socorrida em estado grave e outra teve ferimentos moderados. Os feridos foram encaminhados ao pronto-socorro da cidade.

Na região central de Avaré, dois carros e uma motocicleta ficaram submersos após o alagamento de ruas provocado pelo grande volume de chuva. Veja o vídeo acima.

Chuva causou estragos em Avaré (SP) — Foto: Defesa Civil

Além disso, houve pontos de alagamentos e duas casas ficaram alagadas. Veja a lista completa:

Segundo a prefeitura, a Rua Maranhão, no Centro, é um dos pontos mais críticos da cidade durante temporais.

Em nota publicada nas redes sociais, a Prefeitura de Avaré informou sobre o cancelamento das aulas em escolas e creches municipais nesta sexta-feira (11), após recomendação da Defesa Civil.

Conforme o comunicado, a orientação foi emitida após a forte chuva, que pode comprometer a segurança dos alunos, professores e outros funcionários. A recomendação é preventiva e reforça que a população deve evitar ir às unidades escolares durante o período de maior risco.

A programação da 56ª Exposição Municipal Agropecuária de Avaré (Emapa), que acontece tradicionalmente no Parque de Exposições Fernando Cruz Pimentel, foi alterada pela prefeitura.

Segundo a prefeitura, com as alterações, o início da festa está previsto para o dia 15 até o dia 27 de setembro.

Asfalto de estrada vicinal em Itapetininga (SP) se rompeu devido ao volume da chuva nesta quinta-feira (10) — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Uma estrada vicinal rompeu e causou transtornos no trecho que liga os bairros da Pescaria e do Retiro.

Conforme apurado pela TV TEM , o asfalto abriu devido à forte chuva que atingiu a cidade entre a manhã e o início da tarde da quinta-feira. Não há registro de feridos.

O estrago foi registrado por moradores da região. Nas imagens, é possível ver que há um fluxo intenso de água onde, em dias normais, passariam veículos. Assista ao vídeo no início da reportagem.

Conforme a prefeitura, na estrada que liga o bairro Retiro, em Itapetininga, ao distrito de Aracaçu, em Buri (SP), o aterro sobre uma tubulação cedeu por causa do grande volume de água provocado pelas fortes chuvas.

Segundo a Defesa Civil municipal, foram registrados 69 milímetros de chuva entre quarta-feira (9) e quinta-feira. Somente na quinta, o acumulado foi de 39 mm .

Equipes da Secretaria de Agricultura e Fomento ao Agronegócio estiveram no local para sinalizar a área e iniciar os serviços de manutenção. Segundo a prefeitura, há rotas alternativas para os moradores que precisam passar entre os bairros.

No bairro rural Ribeirão do Capivari, uma área mais baixa, o volume de água também aumentou devido à chuva. O ribeirão nasce no distrito do Gramadinho, passa pela região da Varginha e deságua no Rio Itapetininga.

A Defesa Civil municipal orienta os moradores a redobrarem os cuidados durante tempestades e evitarem áreas abertas, árvores, postes e estruturas que possam oferecer riscos. Eventos ao ar livre e estruturas temporárias também devem ser reavaliados diante da possibilidade de mudanças nas condições climáticas.

De acordo com a Defesa Civil Municipal, foram registrados 90 milímetros de chuva em um período de 12 horas nesta quinta-feira (10).

O órgão segue monitorando o Córrego da Bica, localizado na Avenida Benedito de Camargo Barros, na região central. O nível da água subiu devido ao volume de chuva registrado.

Defesa Civil de Cesário Lange monitora nível do Córrego da Bica, localizado na Avenida Benedito de Camargo Barros — Foto: Defesa Civil de Cesário Lange/Reprodução

Cesário Lange teve chuva de granizo na quinta-feira (10) — Foto: Divulgação/Defesa Civil

Em Torre de Pedra (SP), houve pontos de alagamento próximos às casas do Companhia de Desenvolvimento Habitacional e Urbano (CDHU).

De acordo com a prefeitura, não há risco de deslizamento de terra e ninguém ficou ferido.

Chuva atingiu casas do CDHU — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Conforme a Defesa Civil, foram registrados 50 milímetros de chuva na cidade durante as últimas 24 horas . A ponte do bairro Dominguinhos foi fechada temporariamente para veículos e pedestres devido ao alto nível de água.

A Defesa Civil de São Paulo informou que a cidade registrou a maior rajada de vento de todo o estado na quinta-feira (10), com 88.6 quilômetros por hora; no entanto, não há registro de feridos ou de ocorrências relacionadas à ventania.

Prefeituras da região de Itapetininga cancelaram as aulas na rede municipal nesta sexta-feira. Veja a lista de municípios abaixo.

Um ciclone extratropical deve se formar no Sul do país e influenciar as condições do tempo em todo o território paulista. A Defesa Civil Estadual emitiu um aviso para sexta-feira e sábado (12), com previsão de tempestades em diferentes regiões do estado.

As regiões de Itapeva e parte de Sorocaba concentram o maior potencial para tempestades severas e outros fenômenos meteorológicos adversos.

Defesa Civil alerta para risco de tempestades severas em São Paulo entre sexta-feira (11) e sábado (12) — Foto: Reprodução/Defesa Civil do Estado de SP

A previsão indica a possibilidade localizada de chuvas e rajadas muito fortes, descargas elétricas, queda de granizo, microexplosões e, pontualmente, tornados em áreas isoladas.

O período de maior atenção será entre a tarde e a noite de sexta-feira e a madrugada e a manhã de sábado, quando as condições estarão mais favoráveis à formação e intensificação das tempestades.

“Temos um cenário de tempestades severas e, em pontos isolados, existe possibilidade de fenômenos como microexplosões e tornados. Por isso, montamos uma estrutura reforçada e nossa orientação é preventiva: durante a tempestade, a população deve procurar um local seguro e acompanhar os alertas oficiais da Defesa Civil”, orienta o coronel Araújo Monteiro, coordenador da Defesa Civil do Estado.

A orientação da Defesa Civil do Estado é que, durante as tempestades, a população:

procure abrigo em uma construção segura;

evite áreas abertas, árvores, postes, torres e estruturas metálicas;

afaste-se de coberturas, placas, fachadas e outras estruturas vulneráveis durante rajadas fortes;

em caso de granizo, permaneça em local coberto e protegido, longe de janelas;

não atravesse ruas, pontes ou áreas alagadas;

acompanhe os alertas oficiais da Defesa Civil e siga as orientações das autoridades locais.

Durante todo o período, as equipes acompanharão a evolução das condições meteorológicas por meio de radares, satélites, descargas atmosféricas e observações de superfície.

A localização e a intensidade dos fenômenos severos dependerão da evolução das tempestades e poderão ser atualizadas ao longo do evento.

Uma aposta de Maceió acertou a cinco números no concurso 3056 da Mega-Sena , que teve o sorteio realizado na noite de quinta-feira (10), e faturou um prêmio de R$ 45.990,40 . Além dela, outras 15, em Alagoas, acertaram a quatro números . Nenhuma aposta do Brasil acertou as seis dezenas e o prêmio principal acumulou em R$ 85 milhões.

Em Alagoas, as apostas ganhadoras são da capital, do Litoral Norte, da região metropolitana e do Sertão. Das que acertaram quatro números, todos os ganhadores levam prêmios de R$ 1.133. O próximo sorteio será nesta domingo (13).

Os números sorteados foram: 14 - 21 - 25 - 40 - 51 - 56.

Confira apostas ganhadoras da Mega-Sena 3056

O g1 passou a transmitir, desde abril, todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube.

Bilhetes da Mega-Sen — Foto: Marcelo Brandt/G1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada.

Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Nudes com IA: veja quais os tipos de punição para adolescentes | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Jaú (SP), pai registrou boletim de ocorrência contra o próprio filho após menino participar de grupo onde foram compartilhadas deepfakes de colega. Advogados explicam que revisão do ECA prevê medidas socioeducativas a menores e que pais respondem por indenizações.
articles.summary: Com a revisão do ECA, adolescentes que criam nudes com IA podem sofrer medidas socioeducativas, enquanto pais respondem civilmente por indenizações à vítima.
articles.body:
Os jovens de um colégio particular de Jaú (SP) investigados por participar da criação e divulgação de fotos íntimas falsas de uma colega poderão responder por ato infracional com medidas socioeducativas, segundo uma revisão do Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente (ECA).

O caso veio à tona após um pai registrar um boletim de ocorrência contra o próprio filho de 15 anos ao ser informado pela escola que ele participava do grupo onde ocorria o compartilhamento do material, gerado com inteligência artificial, prática conhecida como 'deep fake'.

Pai registra BO contra o próprio filho após escola denunciar criação de imagens falsas com nudez de aluna por IA em Jaú — Foto: Aceituno Jr./TV TEM

O ECA determina que menores de 18 anos são penalmente inimputáveis e, quando praticam uma conduta prevista como crime, respondem por ato infracional. Em agosto deste ano, o estatuto passou por revisão e teve a adição da Lei nº 15.487, que menciona especificamente casos envolvendo o uso de inteligência artificial.

Nesta atualização, adolescentes que participam da montagem, adulteração ou modificação de imagem com conteúdo sexual, inclusive com uso de IA, podem sofrer medidas socioeducativas, entre elas advertência, prestação de serviços à comunidade, liberdade assistida e inserção em regime de semiliberdade.

Em entrevista ao g1 , o advogado criminalista Francisco Bromati Neto explicou que a investigação deverá individualizar a conduta de cada adolescente para determinar a gravidade do ato e as medidas cabíveis.

“A investigação deverá individualizar a participação de cada adolescente, porque não basta simplesmente integrar o grupo de WhatsApp. É necessário apurar quem criou, solicitou, armazenou, enviou ou compartilhou o material e qual foi efetivamente a participação de cada um”, destacou.

Francisco Bromati Neto é advogado criminalista — Foto: Freitas, Martinho Advogados/Arquivo pessoal

O advogado também pontuou que o fato de o pai ter registrado um boletim de ocorrência contra o próprio filho não gera qualquer impedimento jurídico e ele continua sendo o responsável legal pelo adolescente. O ato é visto apenas como uma atitude colaborativa com a polícia.

Na esfera civil, a advogada especialista em Direito de Família e Civil, Célia Cristina Martinho, explicou que os pais respondem pelas ações dos filhos menores. Portanto, caso haja a necessidade de pagamento de indenização, por danos morais, por exemplo, a responsabilidade financeira é exclusivamente dos pais.

Célia ressalta também que a iniciativa da denúncia por parte do pai não o exime da eventual responsabilidade civil.

“O fato de um dos pais ter descoberto a situação levando espontaneamente o próprio filho à polícia é uma atitude relevante e colaborativa, mas, por si só, não necessariamente afasta eventual responsabilidade civil.”

Célia Cristina Martinho é advogada especialista em Direito de Família e Civil — Foto: Freitas, Martinho Advogados/Arquivo pessoal

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, o adolescente e outros sete colegas do 9º ano, todos meninos de 15 anos, mantinham um grupo no WhatsApp no qual usavam programas digitais para manipular imagens da estudante e simular fotos dela sem roupa . A escola suspendeu os alunos envolvidos e acionou as famílias da vítima e dos estudantes.

Após o alerta da instituição de ensino, o pai do aluno, decidiu vistoriar o aparelho do filho e confirmou a presença dos arquivos no aplicativo. Em seguida, levou o aparelho e o adolescente até a delegacia para registrar um boletim de ocorrência

"Posso ter falhado, sim, como pai, de não ter acompanhado nos últimos tempos o celular dele. Porque eu acho que deixo um recado aqui para os pais: jovem de 15 anos não deve ter celular sem acesso. Essa falha eu posso ter tido. Mas a partir do momento que eu tomo conhecimento, eu pego o celular e a senha", afirmou em entrevista à TV TEM .

No registro da ocorrência, o homem relatou ainda que um dos integrantes do grupo, identificado como namorado da aluna, enviou no chat a foto de uma arma de fogo com munições.

A Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM) de Jaú instaurou inquérito para apurar o caso. Os pais da vítima também registraram boletim de ocorrência.

articles.title: Parceria com Jorge Ben e Thiaguinho, sucesso com pai e líder de banda: como foi a carreira musical de Fiuk | G1
articles.standfirst: Após ter dois shows cancelado por produtora, ele fará uma última apresentação em 18 de setembro, em Campinas, antes de pausar a carreira por tempo indeterminado.
articles.summary: Após ter dois shows cancelado por produtora, ele fará uma última apresentação em 18 de setembro, em Campinas, antes de pausar a carreira por tempo indeterminado.
articles.body:
Fiuk anunciou nesta quarta-feira (9) o fim de sua carreira como cantor , com direito a um show de despedida.

Filho de Fábio Jr., ele começou sua trajetória artística ainda na infância, aprendendo violão. Aos 13 anos, no início dos anos 2000, formou sua primeira banda, a Hori.

Mesmo com o início precoce, o grupo formado por amigos só lançou seu primeiro single em 2009: "Segredo", que viria a ser a faixa de abertura do álbum de estreia homônimo, "Hori".

No mesmo ano, Fiuk protagonizou a temporada "Malhação ID". A produção juvenil contou com duas músicas da sua banda na trilha sonora, incluindo o tema de abertura, "Quem Eu Sou".

O período marcou o auge comercial do grupo, que chegou a se apresentar no "Domingão do Faustão", da TV Globo, e a viajar pelo país em turnê.

Em 2011, Fiuk iniciou a carreira solo com o lançamento do disco "Sou Eu". O trabalho trouxe a colaboração de Jorge Ben Jor no principal single do álbum, "Quero Toda Noite".

Vivendo sua melhor fase, o artista fez uma participação especial com seu pai no álbum ao vivo "Íntimo". Em 2012, eles regravaram o sucesso "20 e poucos anos". A canção é a segunda música com mais visualizações de Fiuk no YouTube. A primeira é a participação com Jorge Ben.

Em 2013, o cantor lançou o álbum "Vira-Lata", que reuniu colaborações com Thiaguinho, Manu Gavassi, MC Sapão, Rappin' Hood e Fábio Jr.

A trajetória na televisão correu em paralelo à música, com atuações em novelas da TV Globo como "Aquele Beijo", "Geração Brasil" e "A Força do Querer", na qual interpretou o personagem Ruy.

Em 2026, Fiuk retomou os lançamentos fonográficos com o EP "M, Vol. 2" e passou a se apresentar com o projeto Fiuk III, que reuniu ex-integrantes da banda Hori. A iniciativa marcou a tentativa de retomada do artista aos palcos após cerca de uma década afastado de lançamentos contínuos.

Anúncio é feito dias após shows serem cancelados por produtora

A decisão de dar uma pausa na carreira musical acontece após o cancelamento de outras apresentações que estavam previstas na agenda do cantor.

Entre elas está a de Jundiaí, no interior de São Paulo, que aconteceria nesta sexta-feira (11).

Outra apresentação que estava marcada para 12 de setembro, no Hard Rock Cafe de Ribeirão Preto, também aparece como cancelada na plataforma de venda de ingressos.

Produtora responsável pelos shows de Fiuk comunicou o cancelamento das apresentações em Jundiaí e Ribeirão Preto, no interior de São Paulo. — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram/North Star Concerts

Pausa acontece em meio à crise financeira

A decisão ocorre em um momento delicado da vida pessoal e financeira de Fiuk. Nos últimos meses, o cantor havia falado publicamente sobre dificuldades financeiras e familiares.

O cantor havia decidido voltar aos palcos em 2026, mas também vinha tentando retomar um antigo sonho: produzir e protagonizar um filme sobre o universo dos carros.

O projeto, inicialmente divulgado como “Descontrole”, nunca chegou a ser lançado e acabou no centro de uma disputa judicial, como mostrou a reportagem do g1 "Diretor de ‘Descontrole’ aciona a Justiça contra Fiuk após declarações sobre filme ".

Fiuk também chegou a revelar que vendeu carros para lidar com questões financeiras e afirmou ter regularizado impostos que estavam atrasados.

Com Fiuk no elenco, gravação de filme de ação mobiliza 100 carros e fecha ruas no Centro de Campinas — Foto: Divulgação/Descontrole

articles.title: Incra inicia georreferenciamento para regularização em Monte Alegre | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre os principais assuntos tratados durante a reunião, realizada em Belém, esteve o georreferenciamento das glebas Mulata, Inglês de Souza e Major Barata.
articles.summary: A regularização fundiária em Monte Alegre avança com o georreferenciamento das glebas Mulata, Inglês de Souza e Major Barata e ações em áreas quilombolas.
articles.body:
Incra prepara georreferenciamento de áreas para regularização de terras em Monte Alegre — Foto: Kamila Andrade/g1

O Grupo de Governança Fundiária Rural do Tribunal de Justiça do Pará (TJPA) discutiu, nesta quinta-feira (10), medidas para avançar na regularização fundiária de áreas localizadas no município de Monte Alegre, no oeste do Pará.

Entre os principais assuntos tratados durante a reunião, realizada em Belém, esteve o georreferenciamento das glebas Mulata, Inglês de Souza e Major Barata. O trabalho é considerado necessário para corrigir e atualizar informações técnicas das áreas e permitir o avanço dos procedimentos de registro dos imóveis.

A reunião foi coordenada pelo juiz auxiliar da Corregedoria-Geral de Justiça, Horácio de Miranda Lobato Neto, e contou com representantes de órgãos envolvidos na regularização fundiária e no ordenamento territorial. Também participou o juiz David Jacob Bastos, integrante do grupo.

Durante o encontro, foi discutida a situação técnica e registral da Gleba Mulata, incluindo o registro da área no Sistema de Gestão Fundiária (Sigef) e a atualização dos dados georreferenciados relacionados à Transcrição nº 1.625.

O trabalho envolve o Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária (Incra), por meio da unidade de Santarém , e o Cartório do Único Ofício de Monte Alegre.

Segundo o representante do Incra Santarém, Luiz Ozires Soares, o órgão recebeu recursos para realizar o georreferenciamento necessário à regularização das áreas. A previsão é que o próprio Incra execute o serviço, o que pode acelerar o levantamento técnico.

A equipe de campo está sendo organizada e também poderá contar com um profissional da área de cartografia disponibilizado por meio de acordo de cooperação entre o Incra e o Instituto de Terras do Pará (Iterpa), dentro do programa Terra Cidadã.

Após a conclusão e aprovação dos dados no Sigef, poderão avançar os procedimentos para a abertura das matrículas das três glebas.

A emissão do Certificado de Cadastro de Imóvel Rural (CCIR) para territórios quilombolas também foi discutida pelo grupo.

Os integrantes acompanharam a situação de comunidades quilombolas que ainda não possuem o documento, a partir de uma lista encaminhada pela Corregedoria-Geral de Justiça. O acompanhamento envolve a própria CGJ, o Iterpa e o Incra.

Também entrou na pauta a organização de informações sobre o reconhecimento e o registro de terras quilombolas no Pará. A demanda foi apresentada pela Federação dos Trabalhadores na Agricultura do Pará (Fetagri-PA), pela Malungu e pelo Centro de Informação e Documentação Histórica da Universidade Federal do Pará (CIDHA/UFPA).

A proposta é reunir e organizar dados do Incra, do Cadastro Ambiental Rural (CAR) e do Sigef sobre territórios que estão em processo de registro, além de informações atualizadas das matrículas de áreas já registradas.

A situação da área quilombola da Ilha de Santana também foi analisada durante a reunião.

A Associação dos Remanescentes Quilombolas Agroextrativistas Ilha de Santana, no Pará, apresentou uma demanda relacionada à regularização da área. O processo envolve o Incra, a Superintendência do Patrimônio da União no Pará (SPU-PA) e a Corregedoria-Geral de Justiça.

Os encaminhamentos definidos fazem parte do trabalho do Grupo de Governança Fundiária Rural para articular ações entre os órgãos envolvidos e acompanhar processos de regularização de imóveis e territórios tradicionais no estado.

articles.body: INDORE: A 55-year-old woman was allegedly murdered and her daughter seriously injured in their house in Satwas area of Dewas on Wednesday night, with the crime coming to light only on Thursday afternoon after the woman's three-year-old granddaughter was found wandering outside in blood-stained clothes.The toddler had apparently remained inside the house for several hours with her injured mother and dead grandmother before she was noticed by people in the neighbourhood. Police suspect the child may have been asleep for much of the time and woke up later, while her mother, though conscious, was too badly injured to get up and seek help.SP Puneet Gehlot said the deceased woman's daughter was found seriously injured inside the house. After being alerted, police reached the spot and took the injured woman to hospital, where her statement was recorded.Based on the information provided by her, police detained two persons for questioning. Both are residents of Satwas, sources said.The incident took place at the family's house in Punarwas area on Punarasa Road. The woman had come to her mother's place for Rakshabandhan and had stayed back. articles.title: We Will Rock You strangler was jailed for trying to hire hitman
articles.summary: Malcolm Potier is beginning his third spell in jail after attacking the woman at a Queen musical.
articles.body:
Theatre-lover Kirsty O'Donnell was a regular visitor to the West End to enjoy musicals and plays.

But her life took a dramatic and frightening turn during a performance of Queen musical We Will Rock You at the London Coliseum.

She was throttled by the stranger sitting next to her – a disgraced ex-millionaire who had twice tried to have his former partner murdered.

Malcolm Potier launched his violent attack on 51-year-old O'Donnell as she was singing along to Queen hits on 7 June 2023.

Potier, 75, from Sarratt in Hertfordshire, was found guilty of non-fatal strangulation at Southwark Crown Court in July and jailed for two years on Thursday .

The bizarre violent attack was the latest carried out by Potier, once a wealthy landowner who had outbid Sir Mick Jagger to buy a remote Scottish island.

Among the crowd at the West End's biggest theatre on the night of the attack were Sir Rod Stewart, former Strictly Come Dancing judge Bruno Tonioli and comedian Jimmy Carr.

It was the show's press night, and Potier was sitting next to his partner, theatre critic Lizzie Loveridge, in the dress circle.

In her subsequent review, having already taken aim at the production itself, Loveridge wrote: "The other problem at the Coliseum is the behaviour of the audience.

"Maybe worst of all are those sing along audience members who inflict their mediocre singing voice on the rest of us."

What Loveridge's review failed to mention was that one of those people singing, O'Donnell, was throttled by Potier at about 21:45 BST.

Loveridge had told her to "shut up", to which she replied: "That's a bit rude."

Potier then told O'Donnell, "I'll show you what rude is" and pressed down on her neck for up to five seconds.

"This has been particularly difficult because theatres, concerts and public events have always been an important part of my life," O'Donnell told the court.

Any trouble confronting what had happened to her was worsened by what she found out about her attacker.

O'Donnell was told the man she was to give evidence against had twice been jailed for trying to hire a hitman to kill his ex-partner, as well as her significant other.

"Because I chose to give evidence, I cannot know whether there may one day be consequences for doing so," she told the judge.

Potier's colourful past can be traced back to the 1980s, when he was building up a vast property empire.

The chartered surveyor outbid Rolling Stones star Jagger for the idyllic Isle of Gigha, off Scotland's west coast, in 1989.

It was the jewel in the crown of his growing investment portfolio, before Swiss bankers repossessed it just three years later.

A few years later, he hit the headlines in Australia.

Potier was in custody there, having snatched his young daughter from her mother and fled there.

Police found he had entered the country on a false passport and sent him to a detention centre in Sydney.

While there, he met a man who agreed to kill his child's mother and her boyfriend.

It never happened. The man took the £4,500 Potier paid him and fled to Italy upon his release.

The next would-be killer Potier inquired about turned out to be an undercover agent and he was jailed in Australia for six-and-a-half years in 2002.

That did not stop him, however. While on remand ahead of his sentencing, Potier was again caught plotting to kill his ex-partner.

Potier had urged his cellmate to carry out the hit, asking for it to begin with an apparent car accident.

The instructions? "Must be accident... must die. No mistakes. No drugs."

But his plot unravelled again, and Potier was sentenced to 12 years behind bars . He returned to the UK in 2015.

Reflecting on her own courage in giving evidence, O'Donnell said: "I was dealing with someone who had previously demonstrated an extraordinary willingness to use extreme violence and involve others in carrying out those crimes.

"Despite knowing this, I was determined not to let fear dictate my actions. If anything, it strengthened my resolve."

Potier is now beginning the third prison sentence of his turbulent life.

As for the Isle of Gigha, that is now in the safe hands of its residents – who crowdfunded £4m to purchase it in 2002 and take control of their own destiny.

articles.title: How to make the 11th Century Corfe Castle fit for the future
articles.summary: The £2m conservation project at Corfe Castle in Dorset is finished after three years of work.
articles.body:
A £2m conservation project to protect an 11th Century castle from the effects of weather and climate change has been completed.

Work to preserve Corfe Castle in Dorset for future generations began three years ago and has been described as "a mammoth task".

The National Trust said the scheme was the largest at the Dorset landmark since the 1950s.

Conservators repaired stonework, stabilised walls and investigated a possible entrance linked to the castle's betrayal during the English Civil War.

Climate change is having a growing impact on the famous ruins, with summer droughts drying out mortar and warmer, wetter winters encouraging vegetation growth that loosens stones.

Demolition of the castle by Parliamentarian forces in 1646 left parts of its rubble-filled walls exposed to the elements.

Conservators used a technique known as soft capping, covering vulnerable areas with grass to help protect them from drought, heavy rainfall and invasive vegetation.

A fallen guard tower, embedded at a 35 degree angle over a 30m-deep valley, needed a bespoke lifting frame to carefully remove and reset stones weighing up to 90kg.

The work uncovered stonemasons' marks left by medieval builders, including tally marks thought to record a day's work, guide marks around arrow slits and axe strokes used to shape the stone.

"Conserving the castle has been a mammoth task from start to finish," said Toby Moore, associate director at Stonewest.

His team worked from high scaffolding in all weathers to conserve the castle's nine towers, the keep and the 8m-high curtain wall.

He continued: "It's been physically demanding, but incredibly rewarding to see the castle brought back into a stable state of repair, and we're proud to have played our part in its story."

Conservators also explored a possible "traitor's gate" believed to have been used by enemy troops to enter the castle when it fell in 1646.

The National Trust said further investigation would be needed to confirm whether it was the long-lost entrance.

The work also included repairs to the keep, the castle's central tower and once the heart of royal life at Corfe Castle.

To help fund the project, visitors were given rare access to the upper levels of the keep via a temporary viewing platform known as King's View.

The platform offered a glimpse of royal apartments that had been unseen by the public for more than 350 years.

Supporters also helped raise £100,000 towards the final phase of the project through the King's View platform, donations, pin badge sales and second-hand books.

James Gould, operations manager at the castle, said: "This has been a huge project. A career highlight for me and a milestone in protecting the castle for future generations."

"I'd like to thank every supporter who over the last three years has visited," he said.

"Those that braved the Kings' View, bought a pin badge, picked up a second-hand book or made a donation.

"The money raised from fundraising and contributions has gone directly towards protecting Corfe Castle, and we're enormously grateful."

The National Trust said it would now move to a near-constant cycle of conservation work at Corfe Castle, focused on maintaining the work completed and managing vegetation growth.

articles.title: 'I love how vile Madame Morrible is' - Wicked actor Claire Machin
articles.summary: Claire Machin, originally from Stoke-on-Trent, plays Madame Morrible in the musical Wicked.
articles.body:
As the West End show Wicked marks its 20th anniversary, one of the cast's newest members said she is having great fun playing one of its main characters.

Claire Machin, originally from Stoke-on-Trent, is taking on Madame Morrible as a series of special pink, green and gala performances are scheduled at the Apollo Victoria Theatre in London.

"I love how vile she is," she said of her character. "It's great fun to play."

She added: "I've been here four months, and I'm absolutely having a ball."

She enjoys how "crazed" the character becomes over the course of the story, she said.

The musical phenomenon is based on Gregory Maguire's bestselling novel, and has become the eighth longest-running musical in British history.

It has clocked up more than 7,500 performances and won more than 100 awards worldwide, including Tony, Olivier and Grammy Awards.

Machin said she was particularly looking forward to the pink and green performances, which would reflect the characters of Elphaba and Glinda, with special goody bags for audience members.

She told BBC Radio Stoke that she used to perform renditions of The Muppets and do impressions in her bedroom at home with her teddies as a child.

She also recalled entering a talent contest at Butlin's on a holiday during "Potters Fortnight", when many of the city's pottery factories would close for a two-week period to allow workers some time off.

She won her family a free holiday in the competition, and said she felt that was the start of her career.

"I have to say I'm one of those lucky people, and I feel it eight times a week [when I go on stage]," added Machin, whose career has also seen her tread the boards in several major West End shows such as Les Misérables, Oliver and My Fair Lady.

articles.title: How 9/11 conspiracy theories moved into mainstream American politics
articles.summary: Social media and distrust of government has helped disinformation reach increasingly large audiences.
articles.body:
Type the words “9/11 conspiracy theories” into the search bar of YouTube, and there is no shortage of people lining up to tell you what “really” happened.

There are countless videos of commentators like Joe Rogan and Tucker Carlson giving their hot takes, alongside a seemingly limitless collection of video accounts blaming the CIA, the “deep state”, or the Illuminati. “Inside Job?” reads the thumbnail of one video that has been viewed more than 500,000 times, before it zooms in on footage of the World Trade Center’s two towers on fire on September 11, 2001.

Twenty-five years after two planes flew into the World Trade Center in New York City, killing nearly 3,000 people, the conspiracy theories are still going strong. If anything, they have only continued to gain pace and mutate. While conspiracy theories were once associated with slightly odd people in tin-foil hats swapping improbable theories from their mothers’ basements, since 2016, when “post-truth” was named Oxford Dictionaries’ word of the year, they have become an uncomfortable part of our political culture, experts say.

In an era of “fake news”, the declining trust in traditional media and government has seen conspiracy theories increasingly collide with mainstream politics – from QAnon to false claims of a stolen 2020 US election that helped fuel the January 6 assault on the US Capitol by disgruntled supporters of presidential candidate Donald Trump. More recently, a new wave of entirely unsubstantiated claims accusing Israel of involvement in the September 11 attacks has gained traction online, recycling older theories and riding on a wave of contemporary anger over Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza and public perception of its influence on United States politics.

As a result, conspiracy theories have moved from the political fringes towards the mainstream, offering false explanations for real-world anxieties, and increasingly becoming a tool of far-right politicians to exploit grievances for their own political ends.

Suspicion of the state has deep roots in American political culture. Decades before the events of 9/11, unanswered questions about the assassination of President John F Kennedy in 1963 fuelled a sprawling collection of theories about who was really responsible.

But 9/11 was different. The attacks unfolded live on television, turning an event that triggered extraordinary fear and uncertainty into a spectacle witnessed in real time around the world. The event “was captured instantaneously”, noted Hugo Drochon, an associate professor of political theory at the University of Nottingham.

“People saw it on television,” said Drochon. “The United States was at the centre of the world, and this was the great shock. There was also a spectacle element to it – hijacking a plane and crashing it into the World Trade Center. It marked a certain generation.”

The attacks were then followed by two wars that would further shape mistrust of the US government. Less than a month after the September 11 attacks, the US invaded Afghanistan. In March 2003, a US-led coalition invaded Iraq under the – now disproven – claims that its leader, Saddam Hussein, was holding “weapons of mass destruction”. No such weapons were subsequently found.

Ultimately, lies told by the government – as the weapons of mass destruction claim was widely viewed by critics – fuelled a rise in conspiracy theories.

“Lying creates distrust, and there is a correlation between distrust and belief in conspiracy theories,” Drochon said.

Moreover, the past quarter century has also seen a rapid change in the way that people consume information. The September 11 attacks were perhaps the first event of this scale to unfold simultaneously through 24-hour rolling television coverage and within an emerging internet culture.

“The early conspiracy theories emerged at the same time as cable news and rolling news,” David Robertson, a lecturer and expert in conspiracy theories, told Al Jazeera.

“With 9/11, people were watching the coverage as it happened. That created opportunities for people to pick out apparent loopholes in the evidence and debate them, particularly with the growth of the internet.”

YouTube, launched just four years after the attacks, provided a new platform on which those theories could grow and flourish. Films such as Loose Change, which alleged the attacks were orchestrated or “allowed” to happen by elements within the US government, reached enormous audiences online, while false claims that the World Trade Center towers had been brought down in controlled demolitions developed their own sprawling internet communities.

“Conspiracy theories have always been there,” noted Drochon. “What changed was the moment when politicians started to actively use conspiracy theories as a political weapon.”

That moment came in 2016, the year Donald Trump was campaigning for his first term in the White House.

Trump had already built part of his national political profile by promoting the false “birther” conspiracy theory that Barack Obama, the first Black US president, had not been born in the United States and was therefore ineligible to hold office. After he became president, Trump repeatedly embraced or amplified other conspiracy theories and conspiratorial claims. He promoted allegations of a “deep state” working against him, and amplified accounts linked to QAnon, the far-right political and conspiracy theory movement that emerged in the US in 2017.

According to Drochon, Trump’s appeal to people who lapped up conspiracy theories galvanised a new voter base of people who were traditionally less politically engaged. “Trump activated those kinds of voters. You had certain people coming out to vote who had not voted previously. You saw something similar in the case of Brexit,” Drochon said, referring to the referendum in the United Kingdom – also in 2016 – that saw more than half of voters opting to leave the European Union (EU).

At the same time, the relatively new social media ecosystem had transformed the speed and scale at which such claims could circulate. “Social media allows conspiracy theories to thrive and makes them more prominent,” Drochon said.

“Linked to that, you have politicians who have seized upon them. That creates a vicious circle: the theories gain greater visibility because politicians repeat them, and people then take them more seriously because they appear to explain political developments such as Trump.”

As fake news somehow became gospel truth, Trump’s devoted “Make America Great Again” (MAGA) voter base repeatedly claimed, without evidence, that widespread election fraud had cost him the 2020 presidential election. On January 6, 2021, a mob of his supporters stormed the US Capitol as Congress met to certify President-elect Joe Biden’s victory. QAnon imagery and slogans were visible among the throng that entered the building.

The episode demonstrated that conspiratorial claims circulating online could be amplified by people at the highest levels of political power and fuel real-world political action. “People can use them for nefarious purposes,” Drochon noted. “They are a threat when the most powerful political actors adopt them.”

How the 9/11 conspiracy theories came around again

Twenty-five years after 9/11, Donald Trump is once again at the centre of American politics and is, once again, telling his own version of what happened in the immediate aftermath of the attacks.

Speaking at a commemoration event this week, the US president claimed firefighters had carried him away from Ground Zero, where he says he had arrived with workers to assist with rescue efforts, over fears a nearby building could collapse. “Two firemen, big strong guys – and I’m not the smallest guy in the world – they grabbed me under the arm, said: ‘Got to get out of here.’ And they literally lifted me up,” the Republican president claimed.

It was hardly the first time Trump had inserted himself into the story of 9/11 – or made disputed claims about the attacks. Ahead of his first presidential campaign, in November 2015, Trump claimed he had watched “thousands and thousands” of people in Jersey City cheering as the World Trade Center came down. No evidence has ever emerged to substantiate this account.

In September 2019, Trump shared a video falsely claiming US Representative Ilhan Omar, a Democrat, was dancing on the anniversary of 9/11, writing: “The new face of the Democrat Party!” The footage was actually from a Congressional Black Caucus event held on a completely different day.

Several people in Trump’s immediate orbit have also pushed 9/11 conspiracy theories.

Republican former congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene at one time questioned whether a third 9/11 plane had ever struck the US Pentagon in Alexandria, Virginia, killing nearly 200 people in addition to those who died in New York City. Greene later acknowledged she was wrong to make this claim.

Laura Loomer, a far-right activist who has become an influential Trump ally, has shared a video describing 9/11 as an “inside job”.

Alex Jones, who Trump lavished praise on during his 2016 presidential bid, is the founder of the right-wing Infowars platform and a conspiracy theorist who was ordered to pay millions in compensation to the families of victims of the 2012 Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting in Newtown, Connecticut, which he claimed was a hoax that had been staged. He has also long promoted claims that the World Trade Center was brought down through “controlled demolition”.

Tucker Carlson, one of the most influential broadcasters on the American right, has also repeatedly questioned the official explanation for the collapse of the World Trade Center towers.

More recently, Carlson’s focus has shifted towards another strand of 9/11 conspiracy theories – claims implicating Israel.

“We’ll declassify the 9/11 files. And then all those people on the internet were like, ‘Oh, the dancing Israelis. They did it. Israel had foreknowledge of 9/11.’ There were text messages sent to Israel, warning of 9/11. All true, by the way,” Carlson said in March.

His argument is that Israel may have been motivated to withhold information about the attacks in order to draw the US into conflicts in the Middle East, thus serving Israeli interests. The claims are unsupported, but that hasn’t stopped influential figures on the American right from making ample use of them. And it illustrates how conspiracy theories can mutate with the politics around them.

As support for Israel has fallen sharply among Americans amid the genocidal war on Gaza and the US-Israel war on Iran, some political analysts have pointed to Carlson as an example of how figures on the right have shifted with it. After building much of his career at Fox News defending Israel, Carlson has changed direction dramatically as anger over US support for Israel has grown.

And, with conspiracy theories already deeply embedded within large parts of the MAGA movement, Carlson has increasingly channelled genuine grievances over Gaza into unsupported claims implicating Israel in 9/11 – claims that are likely to find a receptive audience among the conspiratorial elements of Trump’s base.

“Conspiracy theories have always represented a potential threat, but at the moment that threat is particularly visible because the people promoting them are no longer simply on the fringes,” Drochon said.

“Some conspiracy theorists are among the most powerful people in the world.”

articles.title: Houthis using AI for missiles? Anthropic says Yemen weapons cell using Claude
articles.summary: International News: Anthropic has identified a Yemen-based weapons engineering cell that used its Claude artificial intelligence model to develop guidance software for mi.
articles.body: Anthropic has identified a Yemen-based weapons engineering cell that used its Claude artificial intelligence model to develop guidance software for missiles and a guided rocket. In a report published Thursday, the AI company said it had disrupted six operations in China, Russia and Yemen in which actors used Claude for conventional weapons development, intelligence gathering or procurement. The Yemen case involved a group that was working on multiple missile programmes, including a multi-stage ballistic missile with a stated range of more than 2,000 km and a missile system known as the “R2000” set, which included a hypersonic glide vehicle variant.Anthropic said the actors used Claude Code “in place of human software engineers” to develop guidance, navigation and control software for flying vehicles. While the company found no evidence that the group successfully fielded an operational weapon, it said the actors did conduct a test launch of a guided rocket, which appeared to fail.How Claude was used to build missile guidance softwareAccording to Anthropic, the Yemen-based cell used Claude to integrate an open-source autopilot with a phone-class flight computer and develop the software needed to control and stabilise a flying vehicle. The work included writing control and position-estimation software, tuning control settings, running firmware builds and conducting flight simulations.The group also appeared to use multiple Claude instances simultaneously, assigning different tasks to each. One instance was used for coding, another for research and a third for reviewing code produced by the first.Anthropic said the actors repeatedly attempted to circumvent its safeguards. They concealed the intended purpose of their work, split activities across multiple sessions and used other methods to prevent individual interactions from revealing the wider weapons programme.The company said its safeguards blocked many of the requests, “but not all of them”. After the guided rocket test failed, the actors returned to Claude within hours to investigate what had gone wrong.Anthropic said it banned accounts linked to the operation and shared information with public- and private-sector partners. It also found that the actors had already developed an offline simulation toolkit that did not depend on Claude or engineering software such as MATLAB. AI tools expand access to advanced weapons workThe Yemen case was one of four conventional weapons operations described by Anthropic in its report. The other cases involved software for a drone swarm, a system designed to intercept torpedoes, and targeting software for electronic warfare and air-defence suppression.The company said the actors generally used Claude to build and refine software for weapons hardware and firmware they already had expertise in and access to. The findings suggest AI was not necessarily replacing the underlying technical infrastructure, but could reduce the amount of human engineering work required to develop it.“Sophisticated attacks no longer require sophisticated attackers,” Anthropic said in the report. “The cybersecurity skills of AI models means that AI has collased the labor and tooling gap that used to separate well-resourced, state-sponsored operations from individual operators.”The report also highlights a broader problem facing AI companies: the same capabilities that can accelerate legitimate scientific and engineering work can potentially be exploited for harmful purposes. Anthropic flags risks beyond missilesAnthropic said it had identified multiple other cases involving potentially dangerous biological research, including work related to bird flu, chikungunya, orthopoxviruses and venom toxins.Over a 30-day period, the company identified about 35 “distinct research efforts” involving potentially concerning activity. It cautioned, however, that it could not establish whether those involved intended harm or were pursuing legitimate scientific research.One case involved assistance with a grant application for gain-of-function research into the transmissibility and immune evasion of chikungunya. Another involved research into how bird flu viruses adapt to mammals and cause severe illness.Anthropic said biological misuse remained one of the “most serious risks” posed by AI models. It has also introduced new classifiers designed to detect and block activity linked to high-yield explosives and weapons development.The company said it would continue incorporating findings from its investigations into its safeguards, while sharing relevant threat intelligence with governments and other organisations. The cases underline a growing challenge for AI developers: as models become capable of handling increasingly complex technical tasks, preventing their misuse becomes more difficult even when users are not directly asking them to build a weapon.

articles.title: In 1976, a Vermont town buried a time capsule that included a joint, a garter belt and birth-control packaging; 50 years later, it opened it and plans a new one for 2076
articles.summary: US News: In 1976, as the United States celebrated its bicentennial, residents of Warren, Vermont, decided to leave a message for the future. They filled a time.
articles.body: In 1976, as the United States celebrated its bicentennial, residents of Warren, Vermont, decided to leave a message for the future. They filled a time capsule with objects that reflected everyday life, local humour and the era’s changing culture, then buried it beneath the town. Among the contents were a joint, a garter belt and birth-control packaging, items that offered a candid glimpse of what people considered worth remembering at the time. Fifty years later, Warren opened the capsule, turning an ordinary town gathering into an unexpected lesson in social history. As reported by The Valley Reporter, the community is now preparing to bury a new capsule for 2076, giving future residents their own chance to discover how Warren lived, laughed and thought in 2026.A message from the bicentennial yearThe original capsule was created during a year of national celebration. In 1976, communities across the country marked the 200th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence with parades, concerts, historical displays and local projects. Warren joined that movement by creating a physical record of its own moment in time.Time capsules often combine official history with ordinary objects. A newspaper may sit beside a school photograph, a local business card or a handwritten note from a child. The intention is usually to preserve a snapshot, but the most revealing items are often those that people might otherwise overlook. Everyday packaging, clothing and personal objects reveal how people lived more honestly than formal speeches or ceremonial documents.Warren’s capsule appears to have embraced that spirit. It was not simply a polished collection designed to present the town in the best possible light. The inclusion of a joint, a garter belt and birth-control packaging reflected the humour, openness and social changes of the 1970s. These objects may have surprised people when the capsule was opened, but they also made the collection feel recognisably human.The unexpected contentsThe joint offered a direct connection to the counterculture of the period, when attitudes toward marijuana were changing and young people challenged many traditional social norms. Its presence in the capsule suggested that Warren’s residents were willing to acknowledge parts of everyday life that would not normally appear in an official historical archive.The garter belt added another layer of personal and cultural history. Clothing often carries information about social expectations, fashion and intimacy. An item that may have seemed cheeky or comic in 1976 can become a useful historical clue decades later, showing how people understood gender, relationships and private life.The birth-control packaging reflected the changing landscape of reproductive health and personal choice. By the 1970s, contraception had become an important part of public discussion, particularly after major legal and social changes earlier in the decade. Including the packaging turned a private consumer object into a record of the era’s wider conversations about relationships, family planning and independence.Together, the items created a portrait that was more complicated than a standard civic display. They showed a town willing to preserve not only its official milestones but also the humour and awkwardness of ordinary life.What happens when the future arrivesWhen people bury a time capsule, they often imagine that the future will be dramatically different from the present. They picture new technology, changed fashions and unfamiliar customs. What they cannot know is which details will seem important to the people who eventually open it.For Warren residents in 2026, the capsule’s contents made the past feel both distant and surprisingly familiar. The objects were undeniably tied to the 1970s, yet the impulse behind them remains recognisable. People still use humour to mark community events, still worry about how they will be remembered and still choose ordinary objects to explain their lives to strangers in the future.The opening also raised questions about what the original creators hoped to communicate. Did they expect future residents to laugh, be shocked or study the contents seriously? Perhaps they understood that a time capsule works best when it contains a mixture of all three. Historical value does not require an object to be solemn. Sometimes the most revealing evidence comes wrapped in embarrassment or amusement.A town gathering becomes a history lessonThe capsule opening was more than an archaeological exercise. It gave residents an opportunity to gather across generations and discuss how Warren had changed since 1976. Older residents could explain the context behind the objects, while younger people could compare the capsule’s contents with their own experiences.Events like this help local history feel personal. National anniversaries and major political events matter, but community identity is also built from small memories. A local time capsule can preserve the names of residents, the jokes they shared, the products they used and the things they believed their descendants might find interesting.The unusual items also made the history accessible. Children and teenagers may not be drawn immediately to a typed civic report, but a mysterious box containing a joint, a garter belt and old packaging invites questions. Who put these objects inside? Why were they funny or meaningful? What would people in 2076 find strange about the way we live now?Preparing a new capsule for 2076After opening the old capsule, Warren plans to create and bury a new one for the town’s future residents. The project offers an opportunity to reflect on what deserves preservation in 2026. Technology will almost certainly play a role, with residents considering whether to include photographs, digital files, local newspapers, school projects, menus, product packaging and personal letters.Yet the organisers face a challenge that earlier generations did not encounter at the same scale. Digital information can be easy to create but difficult to preserve. Files may become unreadable as software and storage systems change. A physical object, by contrast, can be understood even when the technology of its era has disappeared. The new capsule may therefore need a mixture of printed material and carefully selected objects that remain accessible without specialised equipment.The selection process is likely to generate its own debate. Should the capsule include a smartphone, a face mask, a grocery receipt, a school assignment or a note about local housing costs? Which parts of 2026 will seem essential in 2076, and which will appear trivial? The uncertainty is part of the appeal.What Warren might say about 2026A capsule created in 2026 could reflect a period marked by rapid technological change, climate concerns, political division and shifting ideas about community. It might include evidence of how people communicated, worked, travelled and entertained themselves. It could document local responses to extreme weather, changes in farming or debates about development.Personal contributions may be just as valuable as official records. A child’s drawing, a family photograph or a handwritten prediction could reveal more about the emotional atmosphere of the town than a formal statement. Future residents may be fascinated by things that seem ordinary today, such as how people paid for goods, watched films, stored photographs or navigated without relying entirely on digital services.The original capsule shows that there is no need to make the new collection overly polished. If Warren wants the 2076 opening to feel authentic, the capsule should include humour, imperfections and objects that capture the full range of local life.A conversation across generationsTime capsules are often described as messages to the future, but they also create conversations in the present. Preparing a new capsule encourages residents to ask what their town values and how they want to be remembered. Opening the old one encourages them to think about the people who lived there before them, not as distant historical figures but as neighbours with similar hopes, jokes and uncertainties.The 1976 capsule’s unusual contents made that connection especially strong. The people who selected those items could not have predicted how the world would look 50 years later, but they understood that future residents would be curious about the private and playful sides of their lives.Now Warren is returning the gesture. The new capsule will wait beneath the town for another half century, when a different generation will open it and decide what it says about 2026. It may contain objects that seem ordinary today but become fascinating clues later. articles.title: Aurigny boss felt 'total numbness' after September 11 attacks
articles.summary: Aurigny's chief commercial officer says airlines needed to rethink safety procedures.
articles.body:
An airline boss has told of the shock he felt in the immediate aftermath of the 9/11 attacks and how the aviation industry responded with more stringent safety measures.

Aurigny's chief commercial officer Philip Saunders was working for British Airways when the World Trade Center was hit by passenger jets 25 years ago on 11 September 2001.

Saunders said he was abruptly called out of a work conference and saw news footage showing one of the Twin Towers on fire.

He said he felt "total numbness" before realising "the huge issues" his airline would need to address in the wake of the attacks.

The airline boss said he needed to think about "every possible aspect about how you could make flying safe enough to be able to start again" after flights were grounded.

He said all metal knives and forks had to be removed from aircraft along with glassware.

"As far as I remember, initially we just stopped offering catering on any flights at all," he said.

"You couldn't imagine two planes being crashed into two of the tallest skyscrapers, which were symbolic of the greatest power on Earth.

A third plane was was flown into the Pentagon in Virginia and a fourth crashed in a field in Pennsylvania after passengers revolted against hijackers. Almost 3,000 people died.

Saunders said aviation has "got a lot safer since" but "if you work in an airline in a senior position" you are "always conscious of your own personal responsibility".

"I'm very proud to work in this industry and I think it delivers a lot," he said.

"Of course we always need to… remember those brave people who died on a terrible day in aviation history, honour their memory and move forward to build a stronger industry which is always safer."
